partner_result.application: Used its physical-pair logarithmic envelope and scalar optimizer H on an unnormalized shear-square remainder; proved exact fragment-mass homogeneity and the target-valid 4+2log8 inequality.

new_results.statement: For shear-coordinate subdensities of masses m3,m4, M=m3m4 and L=min(m4/|a|,m3/|b|), the output subdensity satisfies ||p||inf <= M |c|^-1 H((|c|/|d|)(L/M)^2).

If the dominant shear coordinate remains whole, arbitrary finite/countable fragmentation of the other coordinate preserves the partner density constant exactly before normalization, including remote/unbounded fragments.

target_valid_application: For eigenvalues c,-c,d(1+alpha^2) satisfying |c|>=1 and |d|(1+alpha^2)>=1, each one-sided fragment of mass m_j contributes density at most m_j(4+2log8); summing gives <=4+2log8=8.158883083359672... .
proof_order_obstruction: If both shear coordinates are split independently into N equal-mass pieces, summing the same cellwise analytic majorant gives H(N^2)=4+2log(8N), so that fragment-first proof order has logarithmic loss. This is not a density lower bound or QFORM counterexample.
unresolved_implication: Derive from bare s3(A)>=1 a product-preserving structural reduction exposing a whole dominant smoothing coordinate/bank before localizing the complementary coordinates, or replace the asymmetric shear mechanism by a genuinely joint whole-bank certificate.
next_step: Test the one-sided mass-homogeneous compiler on mixed-hub/grouped-bank reductions where an outside partition varies the non-dominant bank while a dominant projection remains unsplit; seek an additive unnormalized budget forced by the spectral hypothesis.
